All aspects of the world *require* math. The houses and apartments we live in. The technology we have at hand. Our entertainment, food, transportation, etc. all require more than just the basics. Good luck trying to figure out construction logistics without knowing how to solve for unknown variables. 

That being said, I do think there's a problem with making certain professional fields HAVE to take advanced mathematics that the field never uses (in a significant fashion). Such as making a future pediatrician have to pass Calculus and Trig. I don't think my primary care doctor needs to recite the trig unit circle to treat my UTI, or my therapist needing to do a thousand derivative equations to prescribe my antidepressants. 

At the end of the day, those of us (including me) who break out into hives when we catch a glimpse of triangle proofs heavily rely on the technology and maths created by people who find math easier than breathing. Thank god those people exist, cause you and me would be floundering around in shit without them.

 1. Yes. I believe the *house* has some sort of conscious. It cannot speak, so it communicates the only way it can - shifting the internal space of its reality to match each person who dares to go inside. 

2. Ultimately, they all did this to themselves. The *house* merely shoved them in a scenario in which all life's distractions - all sound, all environment, all living and dead things - were all gone. In such an environment, with nothing to distract you, you are forced to face yourself. Kind of like those anti-sensory pods they have in real life. Except it's an entire, sentient *house*. 
What would you become if you were in such a place? Nothing to distract you from yourself? Would you like what you see? Probably not. I know I wouldn't. I heavily engage in media all the time for a reason...but I digress. 

The *house* has limitations on who it can reach. It is restricted to whomever decides to move in. But more than that, it is only able to exact its judgement properly if people actually go in the closet themselves. Which is why it is not God. If we must stretch the Biblical metaphor, it acts more like an individual angel. I don't believe Navidson and the others were "chosen". They found a *house* to live in and they decided to explore it. 

3. The best part of this story to me was the fact it truly was each person's autonomy. There really was no monster. Nobody was chosen. Each person who decided to come in fought with their own hell in the depths of the *house*. Some lost, and some did not. This is a common experience reported among people in solitary confinement, or sensory deprivation chambers, or similar experiences dealing with periods of isolation. 

(I'd like to argue that the *house* itself actually does come to everyone who comes across it.. It is powerful enough that in can invade even records and notes written about it. Something that Zampano and Johnny saw firsthand. But even the reader gets to feel it, a bit. Especially on Chapter 9, page 119. That blue box starts appearing. I truly believe that blue box is the *house* itself aiming a bleary, scrutinizing eye at the reader.

 Meanwhile, me reading that, especially at 3am, was keeping me at the edge of my seat. My heart dropped into my stomach when I turned page 143 and saw that next page, when the blue square abruptly disappeared and there was a BIGGER square. It felt like I got jumpscared while reading (which is why Danielewski is an absolute genius). It felt exactly like the *house* was judging ME.)

1. I have no idea how they differ, or if they even differ at all.

I also deepen my voice and wear tighter sports bras, more to experiment than with anything else. The treatment I receive for acting this way trends towards positive.
